brand.cta_line: Ready to hear it for yourself?

slides.text: Two frequencies go in. Your brain creates a third.

slides.title: Left ear
slides.text: Say 200 Hz plays in your left ear.

slides.title: Right ear
slides.text: And 210 Hz plays in your right.

slides.title: The third tone
slides.text: Your brain perceives a 10 Hz beat that neither ear actually heard.

slides.title: Why it matters
slides.text: That beat sits in the same range as your brain's own relaxed rhythms.

slideshows.caption: This is what binaural beats actually are. Headphones on, and your brain does the rest 🎧

slides.text: A radio executive spent decades researching sound and consciousness

slides.title: Robert Monroe
slides.text: In the 1970s he founded the Monroe Institute in Virginia.

slides.title: The idea
slides.text: Different tones in each ear to bring both sides of the brain into sync.

slides.title: The name
slides.text: He called it hemispheric synchronisation.

slides.title: The legacy
slides.text: Decades later, people still use sound to reach deep meditative states.

slideshows.caption: The research tradition behind everything we do at WealthWave FM 🌊

slides.text: The US Army studied this. The report is public.
An Army intelligence officer assessed a sound based consciousness method called the Gateway Process.

slides.title: The method
slides.text: It used binaural sound to guide listeners into deep, focused states.

slides.title: Declassified
slides.text: The report was released in 2003 and sits in the CIA's public reading room.

slides.title: Read it yourself
slides.text: Search 'Analysis and Assessment of Gateway Process'.

slideshows.caption: Real document. Look it up tonight 📄

slides.text: Your brain has at least four speeds

slides.title: Beta
slides.text: Alert, busy, problem solving. Where most of your day lives.

slides.title: Alpha
slides.text: Calm and relaxed. Eyes closed, mind soft.

slides.title: Theta
slides.text: The dreamy edge of sleep. Vivid imagery, deep meditation.

slides.title: Delta
slides.text: Deep, dreamless sleep.

slideshows.caption: Most of us are stuck in beta all day. Binaural beats are designed to guide you elsewhere 🧠

slides.text: Why manifestation coaches talk about theta

slides.title: The in between
slides.text: Theta is that drifting state right before you fall asleep.

slides.title: Vivid
slides.text: Images feel real and emotional here, not forced.

slides.title: Softer filter
slides.text: The busy, critical voice of the day goes quiet.

slides.title: The practice
slides.text: Many people save their visualisation for this window.

slides.text: The one rule for binaural beats

slides.title: Headphones
slides.text: Speakers mix the two tones in the air before they reach you.

slides.title: Why
slides.text: Each ear needs its own separate frequency.

slides.title: No headphones
slides.text: No third tone. Just sound.

slides.title: Any headphones
slides.text: Earbuds work. Over ear is even better.

slideshows.caption: Save this before your first session 🎧

slides.text: Mistakes people make with binaural beats

slides.title: Too loud
slides.text: Low and comfortable is all you need.

slides.title: Multitasking
slides.text: Scrolling while listening keeps you in beta.

slides.title: Giving up fast
slides.text: Give it a week of regular sessions.

slides.title: Wrong place
slides.text: Never while driving or doing anything that needs your full attention.

slideshows.caption: Number four is non negotiable 🚗❌

slides.text: Solfeggio and binaural beats are not the same thing

slides.title: Solfeggio
slides.text: Specific tones like 528 Hz, played to both ears.

slides.title: Binaural
slides.text: Two different tones, one in each ear, creating a third.

slides.title: Different jobs
slides.text: One is a tone. The other is a rhythm your brain follows.

slides.title: Together
slides.text: Some sessions layer both.

slideshows.caption: Now you know the difference 🎶

slides.text: Set your intention before you press play

slides.title: Why
slides.text: Theta is where the mind wanders. Give it a direction.

slides.title: One line
slides.text: Write it in the present tense, as if it's done.

slides.title: Feel it
slides.text: Picture the moment it's real.

slides.title: Then release it
slides.text: Let the sound carry you. Stop gripping.

slideshows.caption: Intention first. Sound second ✍🏾

slides.text: Can't quiet your mind in meditation? Here's why

slides.title: Your brain hates a vacuum
slides.text: Telling it to 'think of nothing' gives it nothing to hold.

slides.title: So it fills the gap
slides.text: With lists, worries and replays.

slides.title: Give it a rhythm
slides.text: A steady beat is something to follow.

slides.title: The shift
slides.text: Following is easier than forcing.

slides.text: How long should a session be?

slides.title: Starting out
slides.text: 15 to 20 minutes is plenty.

slides.title: Settling in
slides.text: Your brain may take a few minutes to follow the beat.

slides.title: Consistency
slides.text: Short and daily works better than long and rare.
